{"id": "26e2800f-3be3-44e9-9b93-80e718d40be0", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_kfwPIZFAY1kiT8LxZ1o1GE", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: aiml-bedrock-security-assessment\\\\ndescription: \\\\\"Use this skill when the user wants to assess, audit, or review the security posture of Amazon Bedrock generative-AI workloads in an AWS account, across regions or associated accounts. Apply it even when the user does not name a specific control, for example when they ask whether their Bedrock guardrails, knowledge bases, agents, or custom models are set up securely, whether model invocations are logged and encrypted, or for a Bedrock security findings report. Covers guardrail coverage, KMS encryption, VPC endpoints, agent and action-group IAM least privilege, invocation logging, CloudTrail, CloudWatch alarms, and Inspector Lambda scanning. Runs strictly read-only checks and returns severity-rated findings with remediation guidance.\\\\\"\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: apparaka\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Read-only Amazon Bedrock security posture assessment: 31 checks across guardrails, KMS encryption, agent IAM, logging and alarms, with severity-rated findings.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, PREVENTION\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon Bedrock\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Machine Learning, Security\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Amazon Bedrock Security Assessment\\\\n\\\\nAssess the security posture of Amazon Bedrock workloads on AWS and produce a\\\\nconsolidated, severity-rated findings report. **You (the agent) run read-only\\\\nchecks directly** using your AWS API access, then assemble the report. No\\\\ninfrastructure is deployed.\\\\n\\\\nThis is the first domain in a per-domain family of AI/ML security posture skills.\\\\nIt covers **31 Amazon Bedrock checks (`BR-01`..`BR-31`)**. SageMaker, AgentCore,\\\\nand cross-cutting Agentic-AI posture are separate skills, not phases of this one.\\\\n\\\\nGuidance is aligned with the AWS Well-Architected Generative AI Lens and the\\\\nAmazon Bedrock security documentation.\\\\n\\\\n## Scope: what this skill owns vs. defers\\\\n\\\\nThis skill is **one of several** Bedrock/AI-ML skills in this repository. To avoid\\\\ndivergent or duplicated results, it draws hard boundaries:\\\\n\\\\n**Owns** \\\\u2014 *proactive, point-in-time security misconfiguration posture* of Bedrock\\\\ncontrol-plane resources: guardrail coverage and tiers, KMS encryption of models /\\\\nknowledge bases / logs / batch output, VPC private connectivity, agent and\\\\naction-group IAM least privilege, agent guardrail association, security logging\\\\n*presence* (invocation logging + CloudTrail), and abuse/monitoring controls\\\\n(alarms, throttling, Inspector).\\\\n\\\\n**Defers to `bedrock-adoption-readiness`** \\\\u2014 Bedrock *production-adoption\\\\nreadiness*: data-retention/ZDR posture, quota and capacity *headroom* planning,\\\\noperational observability *maturity* (dashboards/metrics depth), and\\\\nbedrock-mantle (OpenAI-compatible) surface. Where a check here touches that\\\\nsurface (BR-20 throttling quota; BR-04/BR-06/BR-30 logging/alarms), this skill\\\\nevaluates only the **security control\\'s presence**, not readiness/headroom depth,\\\\nand says so in the finding.\\\\n\\\\n**Defers to `aiml-access-diagnostics`** (reactive) \\\\u2014 diagnosing *why a specific\\\\nBedrock call was denied* by tracing the authorization chain (`iam:PassRole`, trust\\\\npolicy, permissions, resource policy, SCPs). This skill never diagnoses a specific\\\\ndenial; it reports static IAM *posture* (e.g. an over-broad managed policy\\\\nattached). See \\\\\"Coordinating with aiml-access-diagnostics\\\\\" below.\\\\n\\\\n**Out of scope entirely** \\\\u2014 Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (including\\\\nAgentCore observability, owned by `agentcore-observability-setup`), Responsible AI\\\\nGRC, and OWASP Top 10 for LLM. Do not attempt those checks from this skill.\\\\n\\\\n## SAFETY: read-only assessment\\\\n\\\\nThis assessment is strictly **read-only**. When executing it:\\\\n\\\\n- **ONLY** call `Describe*`, `List*`, `Get*`, `BatchGet*`, and equivalent read\\\\n  operations. NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches,\\\\n  enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource, configuration, policy,\\\\n  guardrail, or IAM entity.\\\\n- Do **not** modify resources to \\\\\"fix\\\\\" a finding. Remediation is reported as\\\\n  guidance only; the customer applies changes separately.\\\\n- Never call a non-`Get`/`List`/`Describe` verb \\\\u2014 including analysis verbs such as\\\\n  `iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails`. The DevOps Agent platform enforces a\\\\n  read-only guardrail that blocks such verbs, and this skill treats any control\\\\n  that would require them as **Prescribe-only** (see below), never as Passed.\\\\n- Treat every account as production unless told otherwise.\\\\n\\\\nIf asked to remediate, first present the findings, then confirm explicitly with\\\\nthe user before proposing any change \\\\u2014 and even then, propose, do not apply,\\\\nunless separately authorized.\\\\n\\\\n## Verify vs. prescribe (determinism contract)\\\\n\\\\nNot every best practice is provable from the control plane. Every check in\\\\n[references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) carries a **Verifiability** classification, and you\\\\nMUST honor it so the report never marks an unread control as `Passed`:\\\\n\\\\n- **Verifiable** \\\\u2014 a read-only `Get`/`List`/`Describe` returns the exact\\\\n  configuration. Emit `Passed`/`Failed`/`N/A` strictly from the returned data.\\\\n- **Heuristic** \\\\u2014 readable, but the verdict is an inference (e.g. IAM\\\\n  least-privilege judged from policy contents). Apply the check\\'s stated rule\\\\n  exactly and **cite the concrete evidence** (policy name, ARN, field value) in\\\\n  `Finding_Details`. If the evidence is ambiguous or the needed read is denied,\\\\n  emit `N/A` with the reason \\\\u2014 **never guess `Passed`**.\\\\n- **Prescribe-only** \\\\u2014 cannot be proven read-only under the DevOps Agent (the\\\\n  required verb is blocked, or no control-plane field exposes the state). Emit\\\\n  `N/A` and put the recommended configuration in `Resolution`. **Never emit\\\\n  `Passed` or `Failed` for a Prescribe-only check.** In v1 this is **BR-12**\\\\n  (stale Bedrock access), which needs `iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails`.\\\\n\\\\nWhen read access is denied for any check, the status is `N/A` (reason:\\\\n`AccessDenied`), never `Passed`.\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nFollow these steps in order, and copy this checklist into your working notes,\\\\nticking each item as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Confirm intent and scope (read-only, accounts in scope)\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Resolve target regions\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Run every Bedrock check per region (BR-01..BR-31)\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Validate findings against the pre-report checks\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Assemble and present the report\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1 \\\\u2014 Confirm intent and scope\\\\n\\\\n1. Confirm the user wants a **read-only** Amazon Bedrock security assessment. State\\\\n   the read-only guarantee above.\\\\n2. This skill runs the Bedrock family (`BR-01`..`BR-31`) only. If the user asks\\\\n   for SageMaker, AgentCore, Agentic-AI, Responsible AI GRC, or OWASP, tell them\\\\n   those are separate skills and stay in Bedrock scope.\\\\n3. Determine which **accounts** are in scope (see \\\\\"Multi-account execution\\\\\"):\\\\n   default is the primary account; if the user names account IDs or says \\\\\"all\\\\n   accounts\\\\\"/\\\\\"the organization\\\\\", scope to those associated accounts.\\\\n4. Record the account ID(s) (`sts:GetCallerIdentity` per account) for the header.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2 \\\\u2014 Resolve target regions\\\\n\\\\nSee [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) \\\\u2192 \\\\\"Region resolution\\\\\". In short:\\\\n- Default: the current/session region only.\\\\n- Explicit list (e.g. `us-east-1, us-west-2`): use those.\\\\n- \\\\\"all regions\\\\\": the union of regions where `bedrock` is available.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3 \\\\u2014 Run the Bedrock checks per region\\\\n\\\\nOpen [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check. Each entry gives the\\\\nread-only API call(s), the pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, **verifiability**,\\\\nresolution text, and a documentation reference URL (an HTTPS link).\\\\n\\\\n**Follow each entry\\'s evaluation logic and API list exactly.** Mind the difference\\\\nbetween the SDK client and the IAM action prefix: Bedrock **prompts, agents,\\\\nknowledge bases, flows, and agent action groups** are called through the\\\\n**`bedrock-agent`** SDK client (e.g. `bedrock-agent` `list_agents`), but their IAM\\\\nactions use the **`bedrock:`** prefix (e.g. `bedrock:ListAgents`). `bedrock-agent`\\\\nis not an IAM service prefix, so never name it in a permission or `AccessDenied`\\\\nexplanation \\\\u2014 say which `bedrock:` action is missing. Using the `bedrock` client for\\\\nthose resources yields a false `N/A`; if one API name is unavailable in the SDK, use\\\\nthe equivalent under the correct client rather than marking the check `N/A`.\\\\n\\\\nProduce one finding per check per applicable region, conforming exactly to the\\\\nschema in [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md), including the `Verifiability`\\\\nfield.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 4 \\\\u2014 Validate findings before reporting\\\\n\\\\nBefore assembling the report, check the findings you produced and fix any that\\\\nfail, re-running the affected check if needed:\\\\n\\\\n1. Every check `BR-01`..`BR-31` has a finding for every applicable region (or\\\\n   once per account for global checks), and every finding has a `Status`.\\\\n2. No `Heuristic` finding is `Passed` without concrete cited evidence in\\\\n   `Finding_Details`.\\\\n3. The `Prescribe-only` check `BR-12` is `N/A`, never `Passed` or `Failed`.\\\\n4. Every `AccessDenied` or ambiguous read is `N/A` with the denied action named,\\\\n   never `Passed`.\\\\n5. A missing `modelKmsKeyArn` or `serverSideEncryptionConfiguration` is reported\\\\n   as \\\\\"AWS-owned key\\\\\", never as \\\\\"unencrypted\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5 \\\\u2014 Assemble and present the report\\\\n\\\\nConsolidate all findings and produce the report described in\\\\n[references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md): an executive summary (counts by\\\\nseverity, by region/scope, and by verifiability), a priority list of High-severity\\\\n`Failed` findings, the full findings table, and a machine-readable JSON block. Do\\\\nnot omit `Passed` or `N/A` findings from the machine-readable output.\\\\n\\\\n## Multi-region execution\\\\n\\\\nSome findings are **global** (derived from IAM or AWS Organizations data) and are\\\\nidentical across regions. Emit each global check **once**, tagged\\\\n`Region: \\\\\"Global\\\\\"`, on the first (primary) region only. All other findings carry\\\\ntheir actual region.\\\\n\\\\nGlobal (emit once, `Region: \\\\\"Global\\\\\"`): `BR-01`, `BR-03`, `BR-12`, `BR-13`. Every\\\\nother BR check is regional. When Bedrock is unavailable in a region, emit its\\\\nregional checks as `N/A` for that region rather than skipping them. In\\\\nmulti-account runs, \\\\\"emit once\\\\\" means once **per account**, because IAM/Org\\\\nposture differs by account.\\\\n\\\\n## Multi-account execution\\\\n\\\\nCross-account access comes from the **Agent Space associations**, not from this\\\\nskill. The DevOps Agent service assumes the read-only monitoring role in each\\\\nassociated account directly \\\\u2014 **do not attempt `sts:AssumeRole` yourself**. See\\\\n[references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) \\\\u2192 \\\\\"Account resolution\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n- **Default:** assess only the **primary** account.\\\\n- **Explicit list:** assess the account IDs the user names; each must be an\\\\n  associated account in this Agent Space.\\\\n- **\\\\\"all accounts\\\\\"/\\\\\"the organization\\\\\":** assess every associated account.\\\\n\\\\nFor each in-scope account, scope every read-only call to that account, set the\\\\n`Account` field on every finding, and emit each global check once per account.\\\\n\\\\n## Coordinating with aiml-access-diagnostics\\\\n\\\\nThis skill (proactive posture) and `aiml-access-diagnostics` (reactive\\\\ndenial-tracing) share a Bedrock config-read + IAM-read surface. To stay\\\\nconsistent:\\\\n- **Ownership:** this skill owns the *point-in-time posture snapshot*;\\\\n  `aiml-access-diagnostics` owns *tracing a specific `AccessDenied`*. If a user\\\\n  reports a specific failing call, hand off to `aiml-access-diagnostics` rather\\\\n  than inferring the cause here.\\\\n- **Shared verify-vs-prescribe model:** both skills use the same rule \\\\u2014 a control\\\\n  that cannot be read under the platform\\'s read-only guardrail is reported as\\\\n  `N/A`/Prescribe-only, never `Passed`. Keep this wording aligned across both\\\\n  skills.\\\\n\\\\n## Notes and limitations\\\\n\\\\n- **Point-in-time:** results reflect configuration at scan time; re-run regularly.\\\\n- **No guarantee of security/compliance:** identifies common misconfigurations\\\\n  against AWS best practices; does not replace formal audits.\\\\n- **Shared Responsibility Model:** assesses customer-configurable controls (IAM,\\\\n  encryption, network isolation, logging), not AWS-managed infrastructure.\\\\n- **Coverage:** Amazon Bedrock only. Other AI/ML services are separate skills.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"references/finding-schema-and-report.md\", \"references/bedrock-checks.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "b9a03f38-f751-4c55-9c61-9e180a1fe261", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_vHn9sKOflK3Yipj0YHMFiR", "content": "[{'text': '# Amazon Bedrock Security Checks (BR-01..BR-31)\\n\\nThis reference lists the 31 Amazon Bedrock security checks. Each check is\\nread-only (list/describe/get only) and reports `Passed`, `Failed`, or `N/A`.\\n\\nEvery check carries a **Verifiability** classification that the report engine must\\nhonor (see `SKILL.md` \u2192 \"Verify vs. prescribe\"):\\n\\n- **Verifiable** \u2014 a read-only call returns the exact configuration; the verdict\\n  is deterministic.\\n- **Heuristic** \u2014 readable, but the verdict is an inference; apply the stated rule\\n  exactly, cite the evidence in `Finding_Details`, and emit `N/A` (not `Passed`)\\n  when evidence is ambiguous or the read is denied.\\n- **Prescribe-only** \u2014 not provable read-only under the DevOps Agent; emit `N/A`\\n  with remediation in `Resolution`. **Never `Passed`/`Failed`.**\\n\\nGlobal checks (`BR-01`, `BR-03`, `BR-12`, `BR-13`) derive from IAM/Organizations\\ndata and are emitted once per execution (per account in multi-account runs);\\nregional checks run in each scanned region that has relevant Bedrock resources.\\n\\n**Classification summary:** Verifiable \u2014 BR-02, 04, 05, 06, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 18, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31 (20). Heuristic \u2014 BR-01, 03, 07, 08, 09, 16, 17, 19, 20, 23 (10). Prescribe-only \u2014 BR-12 (1).\\n\\n---\\n\\n### BR-01: AWS IAM Least Privilege\\n- **Severity:** High\\n- **Scope:** Global\\n- **Verifiability:** Heuristic\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies`, `iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies`, `iam:GetPolicy`, `iam:GetPolicyVersion`, `iam:ListRolePolicies`, `iam:ListUserPolicies`, `iam:GetRolePolicy`, `iam:GetUserPolicy`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when an IAM role or user attaches the broad `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` managed policy. `Passed` only when **both** role-side and user-side policy discovery succeed (`iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies`/`ListRolePolicies` **and** `iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies`/`ListUserPolicies`), Bedrock-permissioned principals are found, and none attach `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` (cite each principal + policy inspected). `N/A` when no Bedrock-related principals exist, or when any of those discovery reads is denied \u2014 role-only visibility cannot show a user carrying the policy, so it is never enough for `Passed`; name the denied action in `Finding_Details`. Do not infer least-privilege beyond the explicit `AmazonBedrockFullAccess`/wildcard rule; ambiguous scoping is `N/A`, not `Passed`.\\n- **Resolution:** Replace `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` with a least-privilege policy scoped to the specific Bedrock actions and resources required.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html\\n\\n### BR-02: Amazon VPC Endpoint Configuration\\n- **Severity:** Informational\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints`, `ec2:DescribeVpcs`\\n- **Evaluate:** `N/A` when Bedrock is not in use in the region, or when the region has no non-default VPC (`ec2:DescribeVpcs`) \u2014 an account calling Bedrock over public endpoints with no VPC-resident workload has nothing to route privately. Otherwise `Passed` when a Bedrock interface VPC endpoint (`bedrock`, `bedrock-runtime`, `bedrock-agent`, or `bedrock-agent-runtime`) exists, and `Failed` (Informational) when none does. Private connectivity is a recommended hardening, not a misconfiguration, so this check never counts toward High/Medium.\\n- **Resolution:** Create Amazon VPC interface endpoints for Bedrock so traffic stays on the AWS private network.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html\\n\\n### BR-03: Marketplace Subscription Access\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Global\\n- **Verifiability:** Heuristic\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies`, `iam:GetPolicy`, `iam:GetPolicyVersion`, `iam:ListRolePolicies`, `iam:GetRolePolicy`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when an IAM policy grants wildcard `aws-marketplace:Subscribe` (or equivalent unscoped marketplace subscription) usable for Bedrock model access; `Passed` when subscription access is scoped to specific products (cite the policy). `N/A` when no principals grant marketplace access or reads are denied.\\n- **Resolution:** Restrict marketplace subscription actions to specific approved model products instead of wildcard access.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-iam-awsmanpol.html#security-iam-awsmanpol-bedrock-marketplace\\n\\n### BR-04: Model Invocation Logging\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when model invocation logging is disabled; `Passed` when logging is enabled to CloudWatch or S3; `N/A` when Bedrock is not in use in the region. (Security-logging *presence* only; observability maturity is `bedrock-adoption-readiness`.)\\n- **Resolution:** Enable model invocation logging to capture request and response data for audit and monitoring.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html\\n\\n### BR-05: Guardrail Configuration\\n- **Severity:** High\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:ListGuardrails`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when no guardrails are configured in a region that uses Bedrock; `Passed` when guardrails exist; `N/A` when Bedrock is not in use in the region.\\n- **Resolution:** Create and apply Bedrock guardrails to enforce content and safety policies on model interactions.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html\\n\\n### BR-06: AWS CloudTrail Logging\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `cloudtrail:ListTrails`, `cloudtrail:GetTrail`, `cloudtrail:GetTrailStatus`, `cloudtrail:GetEventSelectors`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when no active CloudTrail trail captures Bedrock API calls; `Passed` when a logging trail covers the Bedrock control plane; `N/A` when Bedrock is not in use in the region.\\n- **Resolution:** Configure an active CloudTrail trail (logging enabled) that records Bedrock management events.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/logging-using-cloudtrail.html\\n\\n### BR-07: Prompt Management\\n- **Severity:** Low\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Heuristic\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:ListPrompts`, `bedrock:GetPrompt`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` only when managed prompts exist but none carry a version (all are `DRAFT`, no numbered version) \u2014 a deterministic proxy for \"version control\". `Passed` when at least one versioned prompt variant exists (cite the prompt ID/version). `N/A` when no prompts are defined. Do not judge subjective \"template quality\".\\n- **Resolution:** Adopt Bedrock Prompt Management with versioned templates and variants for consistent, governed prompts.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.html\\n\\n### BR-08: Agent AWS IAM Configuration\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Heuristic\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:ListAgents`, `bedrock:GetAgent`, `iam:ListRolePolicies`, `iam:GetRolePolicy`, `iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when an agent execution role attaches `AdministratorAccess`/`*FullAccess` or an inline statement with `Action:\"*\"` or `Resource:\"*\"` on write actions (cite role + statement). `Passed` when every agent role is inspected and none match. `N/A` when no agents exist or role reads are denied.\\n- **Resolution:** Scope each agent execution role to the minimal actions and resources the agent requires.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html\\n\\n### BR-09: Guardrail AWS IAM Enforcement\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Heuristic\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:ListGuardrails`, `iam:ListRolePolicies`, `iam:GetRolePolicy`, `iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when invoke-capable Bedrock policies exist but none carry a `bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier` condition key; `Passed` when an IAM condition requires a guardrail on invocation (cite the policy/condition). `N/A` when no guardrails or invoke policies exist, or reads are denied.\\n- **Resolution:** Add IAM condition keys that require an approved guardrail identifier on model invocation actions.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-permissions-id.html\\n\\n### BR-10: Invocation Log Encryption\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration`, `s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration` (IAM action for the S3 `GetBucketEncryption` operation)\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when the S3 destination for invocation logs is not encrypted with AWS KMS; `Passed` when logs are KMS-encrypted; `N/A` when invocation logging is not enabled.\\n- **Resolution:** Enable AWS KMS encryption on the S3 bucket that stores Bedrock invocation logs.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html\\n\\n### BR-11: Flows Guardrails\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:ListFlows`, `bedrock:GetFlow`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when a Bedrock Flow has no guardrail attached to its prompt nodes; `Passed` when flows enforce guardrails; `N/A` when no flows exist in the region.\\n- **Resolution:** Attach guardrails to the prompt nodes of each Bedrock Flow.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/flows-guardrails.html\\n\\n### BR-12: Stale Bedrock Access\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Global\\n- **Verifiability:** Prescribe-only\\n- **Read-only APIs:** *(none reachable)* \u2014 determination requires `iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails` then `iam:GetServiceLastAccessedDetails`. `GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails` is a `Generate*` verb blocked by the DevOps Agent read-only guardrail, so the state cannot be read here.\\n- **Evaluate:** **Always `N/A`** under the DevOps Agent, with `Finding_Details` stating the platform read-only guardrail blocks the required analysis call. **Never emit `Passed` or `Failed`.** Do not call `GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails`.\\n- **Resolution:** Out of band (e.g. IAM console \u2192 Access Advisor, or a Lambda with `iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails`), review last-accessed data for Bedrock-permissioned principals and remove permissions unused for 90+ days.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_last-accessed.html\\n\\n### BR-13: Cross-Account Guardrails Enforcement\\n- **Severity:** High\\n- **Scope:** Global\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `organizations:DescribeOrganization`, `sts:GetCallerIdentity`, `organizations:ListRoots`, `organizations:ListPolicies`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when organization-level Bedrock policies (`BEDROCK_POLICY` type) are not enabled/attached at the org root; `Passed` when Bedrock policies enforce centralized guardrails; `N/A` when not run from the Organizations management account (cite that reason).\\n- **Resolution:** Enable the Bedrock policy type in AWS Organizations and attach Bedrock policies at the organization root for centralized enforcement.\\n- **Reference:** https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_bedrock.html\\n\\n### BR-14: Guardrail Tier Validation\\n- **Severity:** Medium\\n- **Scope:** Regional\\n- **Verifiability:** Verifiable\\n- **Read-only APIs:** `bedrock:ListGuardrails`, `bedrock:GetGuardrail`\\n- **Evaluate:** `Failed` when a guardrail uses the `CLASSIC` content-filter tier;
